title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licensing qualifications and documented controls are supported. Both API calls match their Microsoft references, and independent searches confirmed the narrowly stated documentation gaps.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target date is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is April CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "April CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview as release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) is the only listed cloud; US Government clouds are not listed.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Web is the only platform listed in the roadmap record.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap associates this feature with Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365) and Microsoft Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)", "Microsoft Copilot Studio"]

claims.claim: The agent node hands a workflow step to an AI agent that can reason.
claims.quote: The agent node lets a flow hand a step over to an AI agent that can reason, call tools, and pull from knowledge sources before returning a result.

claims.claim: The agent can call tools within the workflow step.
claims.quote: Equip the agent with tools (Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and connectors) so it can take action.

claims.claim: The agent can read knowledge sources before returning a result.
claims.quote: The agent node lets a flow hand a step over to an AI agent that can reason, call tools, and pull from knowledge sources before returning a result.

claims.claim: The response becomes dynamic content available to subsequent workflow steps.
claims.quote: The agent response then becomes available as dynamic content that you can use in any subsequent step.

claims.claim: A maker adds the node in Copilot Studio through Workflows, an existing workflow's Build tab or a new workflow, and the Agent icon on the Add panel.
claims.quote: In Copilot Studio, go to Workflows and open an existing workflow, or create a new one. Existing workflow: Open the workflow and go to the Build tab. Select the Agent icon on the Add panel.

claims.claim: An existing agent can be selected from a list of published agents.
claims.quote: An existing agent: Select a published agent from a list.

claims.claim: An existing agent runs with its previously configured instructions.
claims.quote: The agent runs with whatever instructions, tools, and knowledge it was already configured with.

claims.claim: An existing agent runs with its previously configured tools.
claims.quote: The agent runs with whatever instructions, tools, and knowledge it was already configured with.

claims.claim: An existing agent runs with its previously configured knowledge.
claims.quote: The agent runs with whatever instructions, tools, and knowledge it was already configured with.

claims.claim: New agent for this workflow creates an inline agent whose instructions, tools, knowledge and output shape are configured in the node and travel with the workflow.
claims.quote: New agent for this workflow: Build an inline agent scoped to this workflow. The agent's instructions, tools, knowledge, and output shape are configured in the node itself and travel with the workflow.

claims.claim: An inline agent cannot be reused outside its workflow.
claims.quote: Can the inline agent be reused outside this workflow? No. An inline agent is scoped to its workflow.

claims.claim: MCP servers can be attached as tools.
claims.quote: You can attach two kinds of tools: Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers: Prebuilt servers that expose a curated set of capabilities.

claims.claim: Any Power Platform connector action can be attached as a tool.
claims.quote: Connectors: Any Power Platform connector action.

claims.claim: Tools and knowledge are optional attachments for an inline agent.
claims.quote: Give the node an instruction, optionally attach tools and knowledge, and you're done.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Public websites can ground the inline agent's answers.
claims.quote: Public websites: Index one or more public URLs so the agent can cite content from those sites.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: SharePoint can ground the inline agent's answers.
claims.quote: SharePoint: Connect to a SharePoint site, library, or specific document so the agent can answer from internal content.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The agent decides at run time which attached tools to call.
claims.quote: The agent decides at run time which of its attached tools to call, in what order, and with what arguments.

claims.claim: The agent decides the order of its tool calls.
claims.quote: The agent decides at run time which of its attached tools to call, in what order, and with what arguments.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The agent decides the arguments to its tool calls.
claims.quote: The agent decides at run time which of its attached tools to call, in what order, and with what arguments.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Turning on Work IQ permits grounding in the running user's recent mail, Teams, calendar, OneDrive and SharePoint context.
claims.quote: Turn on Work IQ to let the agent use the running user's recent work activity, including mail, Teams, calendar, OneDrive, and SharePoint context, to ground its responses.

claims.claim: Request human assistance when unsure is a maker-selected per-node setting.
claims.quote: Turn on Request human assistance when unsure to let the agent escalate when it isn't confident enough to act on its own.

claims.claim: Human assistance emails the connection owner for input.
claims.quote: The agent emails the connection owner for input and waits for a reply before continuing.

claims.claim: An escalation waits for a reply before continuing.
claims.quote: The agent emails the connection owner for input and waits for a reply before continuing.

claims.claim: Structured output exposes agent-written fields to downstream workflow actions.
claims.quote: When you pick a structured output, each field becomes its own dynamic-content token that downstream actions can reference directly.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Without tools the agent can only read and reason, while tools let it act.
claims.quote: Without tools, the agent can only read and reason. With tools, it can also act.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Agent output can drive downstream emails, Teams messages and Dataverse writes.
claims.quote: Insert a text response into an email body, Teams message, or document. Branch the workflow on a structured field such as priority == "high". Write structured fields to Dataverse, Excel, or a SharePoint list.

claims.claim: Evaluations are available only for new agents created in workflows.
claims.quote: Evaluations are only available for new agents created in workflows.

claims.claim: Evaluations are limited to 20 per agent node per day.
claims.quote: You can run up to 20 evaluations per agent node per day.

claims.claim: The node's Learn page does not identify which part of the node feature is still in preview.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio workflow agent node Copilot Credits rate monthly agent limits connector identity credentials preview'; opened agent-node-workflow and read the complete article, including limitations. No preview/GA division is stated.

claims.where: controls[3]; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No tenant UI or API switch dedicated to turning the agent node off is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'agent node disable admin tenant switch' and 'Copilot Studio workflow agent node disable tenant admin switch Power Platform API Dataverse Request human assistance when unsure'; opened agent-node-workflow, flows-overview and manage-usage-github-copilot-harness. No dedicated switch found.

claims.claim: The node is user-opt-in: a maker chooses to add it in the workflow designer.
claims.quote: In Copilot Studio, go to Workflows and open an existing workflow, or create a new one. Select the Agent icon on the Add panel. The configuration panel opens for the agent node.

claims.claim: No node-dedicated administrative switch for the node's knowledge or Work IQ settings is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'agent node Work IQ admin disable knowledge policy'; opened agent-node-workflow, add-work-iq, admin-data-loss-prevention and policy-governance-mcp. They document maker settings and general policies, not a node-dedicated administrative switch.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The agent node article does not specify whose credentials its connector actions or attached SharePoint knowledge use.
claims.quote: Searched: 'agent node credentials workflow'; read agent-node-workflow in full. It identifies the escalation recipient and Work IQ context, not connector/knowledge execution credentials.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies govern Power Platform connector tools in Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks tools in connected MCP servers that rely on them.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced Connector Policies govern certified connectors.
claims.quote: Advanced connector policies currently apply to certified connectors only.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced Connector Policies support MCP server-level blocking.
claims.quote: Within advanced connector policies, administrators can see MCP servers listed alongside other connector types and can choose to block an entire MCP server.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Custom and HTTP connectors still require classic data policies rather than ACP.
claims.quote: Custom connectors and HTTP connectors aren't yet supported. They're planned as a separate rule type in the future. For governing custom connectors and HTTP connectors today, continue using classic data policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Connector operations are governed by the hosting environment's effective policy.
claims.quote: At runtime, when a connector operation is invoked, it queries the effective policy for the current hosting environment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Copilot Studio ACP design-time enforcement is rolling out, with runtime-only enforcement until available.
claims.quote: Design-time enforcement is rolling out across maker portals in the following order: Power Automate maker portal; Copilot Studio; Power Apps maker portal. Until design-time support is available in a given maker portal, ACP operates as a runtime-only enforcement for that workload.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Policy-blocked tools, connectors, models and skills appear disabled in harness-agent selection lists.
claims.quote: When a data policy or Advanced Connector Policy blocks a tool, connector, AI model, or skill, that item appears disabled wherever you'd normally select it, such as the tools list, model list, or skills list.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ in Copilot Studio uses Work IQ MCP, centrally governed in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: using Work IQ MCP tools ... Centralized governance: Admins manage Work IQ MCP in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP administrative policy controls are available only where offered.
claims.quote: The ability to allow or disallow tooling and MCP servers in the Microsoft 365 admin center might not be available in your region yet.

claims.where: Governance controls: Work IQ MCP policy path
claims.claim: The tenant policy is reached in Microsoft 365 admin center through Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy when available.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP tenant policy can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests.
claims.quote: It adds a request-time governance layer that can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests based on tenant policy.

claims.claim: Request human assistance when unsure is conditional escalation, not mandatory approval of every action.
claims.quote: Turn on Request human assistance when unsure to let the agent escalate when it isn't confident enough to act on its own.

claims.claim: Workflow results can vary when actions use AI.
claims.quote: Results can vary when actions use AI or retrieve changing data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Exhaustion of prepaid environment capacity blocks new workflow runs until capacity is available.
claims.quote: Once you fully consume your environment's prepaid Copilot Studio capacity, new workflow runs are blocked until capacity is available.

claims.claim: Already running workflows complete normally when prepaid capacity is exhausted.
claims.quote: Running workflows complete normally.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is consumption, metered in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits. Creating and using agents, workflows, and apps consumes credits based on usage and rate of consumption.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing includes LLM tokens.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing includes tools, knowledge and MCPs.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing includes the harness itself.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Billing starts when makers start building rather than only after publication.
claims.quote: Unlike the standard harness, which starts billing after publish, the Microsoft Copilot harness charges credits from the moment you start building.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Testing and evaluating an agent node can consume credits.
claims.quote: Experiences such as creating an automated solution with natural language, previewing and testing an agent, and generating and creating agent evaluations all consume credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Workflows consume Copilot Studio capacity for each action executed.
claims.quote: Workflows consume Copilot Studio capacity for each action they execute.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A Microsoft 365 Copilot licence covers workflows run inside a standard harness agent by a licensed user.
claims.quote: | Workflows | Yes, when run inside a standard harness agent by a licensed user | Billed in all other cases. |

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Workflows are billed in all other cases.
claims.quote: | Workflows | Yes, when run inside a standard harness agent by a licensed user | Billed in all other cases. |

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No Copilot Credit rate specific to the agent node is published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'agent node rate Copilot'; opened billing-credit-overview and manage-usage-github-copilot-harness; read requirements-messages-management excerpts. No node-specific rate found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Credits are charged to the environment where the work runs.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs, from prepaid capacity or through the environment's pay-as-you-go billing plan

claims.claim: Environment credit consumption can use prepaid capacity or a linked pay-as-you-go plan.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs, from prepaid capacity or through the environment's pay-as-you-go billing plan

claims.claim: Credits are not charged to individual makers.
claims.quote: and not to the individual makers or users who run agents.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Allocating credits and disabling tenant-pool draw contains an environment's prepaid consumption at its allocation.
claims.quote: Clear this option to cap prepaid consumption at the environment's allocation. If the environment has no allocation, it can't consume prepaid capacity from the tenant pool.

claims.claim: Disabling tenant-pool draw does not stop consumption through a linked pay-as-you-go plan.
claims.quote: If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.claim: Azure budgets send alerts without stopping consumption.
claims.quote: Azure budgets and alerts send notifications but don't stop Copilot Studio consumption.

claims.claim: Environment capacity controls apply across Copilot Studio workloads, rather than only workflows with agent nodes.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness. Configure controls with the other Copilot Studio agents, workflows, and features in mind for each environment.

claims.claim: Capacity management requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: The node article names no licence among its prerequisites for adding the node.
claims.quote: Searched: agent-node-workflow article for licence/license and prerequisites; read its complete Add an agent node instructions and billing note. It names no prerequisite licence; product billing is separately documented in billing-credit-overview and manage-usage-github-copilot-harness.

claims.claim: The tenant-draw setting is at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Licensing. Under Products, select Copilot Studio. Select Manage Copilot Credits. Select the environment. Enter the number of Copilot Credits to allocate. Under Capacity overages, clear Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 sets MCSMessages allocation quantity and TenantPool enforcement enabled false.
claims.quote: $apiVersion = "2024-10-01" ... Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put ... "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion" ... entitlementId = "MCSMessages" ... allocation = @{ quantity = 5000 } ... @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false }

claims.where: Governance controls: allocation call authorisation and content type
claims.claim: The allocation request uses authenticated authorisation and application/json content type.
claims.quote: $headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $($auth.AccessToken)" }; -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody

claims.claim: The illustrated allocation body nests environmentId in scope and entitlementId, allocation.quantity and enforcementRules in allocatedEntitlements.
claims.quote: scope = @{ environmentId = $environmentId }; allocatedEntitlements = @( @{ entitlementId = "MCSMessages"; allocation = @{ quantity = 5000 }; enforcementRules = @( @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false } ) } )

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio exposes Agent flow actions used by each workflow.
claims.quote: In the Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio, review the Agent flow actions used by each workflow.

claims.claim: The printed GET environment resources call with MCSMessages, fromDate, toDate and api-version=2024-10-01 retrieves entitlement snapshots.
claims.quote: GET https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/entitlements/{entitlementId}/environments/{environmentId}/resources?fromDate={fromDate}&toDate={toDate}&api-version=2024-10-01

claims.claim: The environment resources entitlement insight operation is deprecated.
claims.quote: Get environment resource entitlement snapshots for an entitlement (deprecated).

claims.claim: The environment resources reference does not promise a workflow-level breakdown.
claims.quote: Searched: get-environment-resources reference for workflow and breakdown; read its complete parameters and response definitions. It documents resources, resourceId, consumed and metadata, not a promised workflow-level breakdown.

claims.claim: The escalation control is at Copilot Studio (maker) > Workflows > workflow > Build > Add panel > Agent > Request human assistance when unsure.
claims.quote: In Copilot Studio, go to Workflows and open an existing workflow, or create a new one. Existing workflow: Open the workflow and go to the Build tab. Select the Agent icon on the Add panel. Turn on Request human assistance when unsure

claims.claim: No documented API equivalent sets Request human assistance when unsure on the agent node.
claims.quote: Searched: 'agent node human assistance API Dataverse table' and 'Request human assistance when unsure enforce API'; read returned node articles and Dataverse bot excerpts. No operation or property for this setting found; agent-node-workflow documents the designer setting.

claims.claim: No central enforcement setting for Request human assistance when unsure is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Request human assistance when unsure enforce API' and 'Copilot Studio workflow agent node disable tenant admin switch Power Platform API Dataverse Request human assistance when unsure'; read node articles and manage-usage-github-copilot-harness. No central enforcement setting found.

claims.claim: Individual monthly agent limits are managed under Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio > Manage Agents.
claims.quote: In the Power Platform admin center, go to Licensing > Copilot Studio. Select Manage Agents. Select the agent, and then select Set limit. Enter the monthly Copilot Credit limit.

claims.claim: Learn does not state that monthly agent limits cap an agent node's credits inside a workflow.
claims.quote: Searched: 'agent node monthly limit credits'; read manage-usage-github-copilot-harness and returned manage-copilot-studio-copilot-credits-capacity and govern-credit-consumption excerpts. These describe agent limits and separate flow enforcement, not a limit on a workflow's agent node.

claims.claim: Tenant-pool draw is selected by default in eligible Copilot Studio environments without allocation configuration.
claims.quote: For eligible Copilot Studio environments, Draw from the available capacity in my tenant is selected by default when no allocation configuration exists.

claims.claim: A published environment group rule governing tenant draw makes the environment setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center

claims.claim: Programmatic requests cannot override the group-governed tenant-draw setting.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.claim: Existing Copilot Studio and environment permissions control who can build.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot harness doesn't have its own maker-access setting. To control who can create agents, use your existing Copilot Studio and environment permissions.

claims.claim: The Workflows page has a Credit usage (last 30 days) column showing each workflow's consumption.
claims.quote: The Credit usage (last 30 days) column shows the credits that a workflow consumed during the last 30 days.
